question: A 72-year-old male visits his gastroenterologist for a check-up one year following resection of a 2-cm malignant lesion in his sigmoid colon. Serum levels of which of the following can be used in this patient to test for cancer recurrence?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Resection of malignant lesion in sigmoid colon" -> "Possible cancer recurrence" -> "Monitoring tumor markers" -> 70% CHAIN: "Resection of malignant lesion in sigmoid colon" -> "Increased risk for cancer recurrence" -> "Monitoring tumor markers" -> 80% CHAIN: "Resection of malignant lesion in sigmoid colon" -> "Check-up for cancer recurrence" -> "Monitoring tumor markers" -> 70%
analysis: Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) is a tumor marker commonly used to monitor for cancer recurrence in patients with a history of colorectal cancer. It is particularly useful in monitoring patients following resection of colorectal cancer, such as in this case.
